rule_or_pattern: In greek_poly lines: a word-initial capital Greek vowel with no breathing, followed by a lowercase Greek letter (regex (?:^|[\s(«\[])[ΑΕΗΙΟΥΩ](?=[α-ωάέήίόύώϊϋΐΰἀ-ᾯὰ-ώᾳῃῳ])), i.e. the print's spacing breathing ᾿/῾ was dropped
notes: This is a 1928 school edition of Cicero's Pro Milone: Latin text with a polytonic Greek commentary and translation. The Latin lines (5, 6, 14, 23, 24) and mixed lines (7, 10-12, 25, 26, 37) are read correctly, so the Latin share is genre, not error. The one recurring fault: when the print has a spacing breathing before a capital (᾿Ε, ᾿Ι), Google sometimes drops it entirely (8 'Ιανουαρίου', 32 'Εσφαλμένως'/'Εμφυλ.', 40 'Ετρουρίᾳ'). Those lines would teach breathing-less capitals; elsewhere breathings are kept as ᾿Α (covered by the pool rule). Isolated misreads: 36 'ἱνὰ' for '[νὰ'.
